newsitem.title: FRANCE: Accor rises on Morgan Stanley note.
newsitem.headline: Accor rises on Morgan Stanley note.

text.p: Shares in French hotels company Accor rose sharply on Friday, bucking a falling market, with traders attributing the climb to Morgan Stanley's strong buy recommendation and putting it on its "fresh money buy" list.
The stock firmed 1.89 percent to 810 francs on volume of 113,592 shares at 1200 GMT.

Morgan Stanley analyst Floreis van Dijkum said Accor was an "attractive investment opportunity". The stock is trading at a 30 percent discount to the European hotel sector on an adjusted earnings-per-share basis. It also stands to benefit from European economic recovery this year, he said.
"With European growth in GDP this year, hotels should do well," he said.

The shares should benefit from management changes and restructuring, following the appointment of Jean-Marc Espalioux as chairman, who has already said the group is selling its 11.5 percent stake in Compass Plc, signalling the disposal of non-core assets.

The fragmented European hotel sector is expected to undergo consolidation, with Accor, as the largest owner and operator in the region, well placed to buy assets from private owners. Currently less than 10 percent of the European sector is quoted compared to 60 percent in the United States, van Dijkum said.

Morgan Stanley has set a target price of 960 francs per share. Despite rising 20 percent since the start of the year, the stock has lagged the CAC-40 index over the one, two and five-year period. "It's got much more to go," he said.
